selection_rule: Best of initial three; replace on two paired wins and mean gain >= 0.002

proposal.reason: Trial 1 used word-only logistic regression with C=0.3 and achieved macro_f1 0.4843, but class recall was [1.0, 0.0187], indicating the spam class is almost never recovered. A word+char representation with C=3.0 is a reasonable next primary-split experiment because char n-grams can capture obfuscated spam patterns and lower regularization may allow the model to fit minority-class signal better than the heavily regularized word-only baseline.
proposal.review: The only completed primary trial is single_word_C0.3. Its high ham recall and near-zero spam recall make macro_f1 the limiting metric. This candidate changes representation and regularization together, so it is an improvement-oriented probe rather than a clean causal test of either factor alone. No confirmation-split measurements are available or compared.
proposal.hypothesis: Combining word and character n-gram features with C=3.0 will provide more discriminative signal for spam-like messages than word-only C=0.3, potentially raising spam recall and therefore macro_f1 on the primary split.
proposal.uncertainty: The direction and magnitude of macro_f1 change are unknown. The candidate changes two factors at once, so any observed effect cannot be attributed cleanly to representation versus regularization. The primary split is small and trial 1's near-zero spam recall may reflect class imbalance or feature limitations; this experiment is exploratory.
